content.comment_body: Hello, does anyone have quick and clear instructions for installing the full version of [product_name] [version_no] on a notebook that doesn't have a DVD drive? My computer has just been reset with Windows 10 Pro, and I don't recall how the installation was done three years ago. I have the original DVD for [product_name] [version_no] along with a USB cable, but my device does not have a DVD drive.

Copy the entire CD/DVD to a USB stick using a computer that has a DVD/CD drive. Then install [product_name] from the USB stick on your new machine. There is no copy protection for [product_name]. Upgrade to [product_name] [version_no] from the [company_name] website: [url]. You need to register first, after which you'll receive an email with the download link.

You will need access to another computer with a DVD drive. Use a program like Power ISO to create an .ISO image file of your [product_name] DVD. Once the .ISO file is created, copy it to a USB flash drive. Insert the flash drive into your notebook, then use Power ISO (or similar software) to mount the ISO file as a virtual drive. Browse to the virtual drive and run the setup program for [product_name]. After installing [product_name] [version_no], you can later upgrade to newer versions. I wish you success with the installation process. Power ISO is just one example; you can use any tool that can create DVD image files and mount virtual drives.

Thank you for your reply. I used an external DVD drive and put in the original [product_name] DVD. Once the setup started, a Java Application Exception occurred: ZeroGu3: Windows DLL failed to load, followed by several lines of stack trace. The installation stops at this point.
Thanks. I tried the upgrade registration process. We also contacted our local [company_name] representative to resolve the issue.

For Java-related errors, try uninstalling any old Java versions from the notebook and then download and install the latest version. If that doesn’t solve the problem, try adjusting the compatibility settings of the [product_name] setup file, such as setting it to run in Windows 7 mode.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced issues installing [product_name] on Windows 10 laptops without DVD drives, even though they had the original DVD and USB cable. Lack of a physical DVD drive and compatibility problems, like a Java DLL error, caused confusion. The thread shows unclear upgrade procedures and reliance on old installation media, making the installation process challenging on newer computers.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easy, dependable method to install and upgrade [product_name] to the latest fully working version on modern notebooks without needing special hardware. They also want the installation to be free from confusing compatibility or Java errors.
